name: Puppeteer
tagline: Probes a running program's variables and fakes data on the fly, so frontend work can continue without a backend.

awards: Warp: Best Developer Tool by Warp

problem: Frontend engineers stall when the backend they depend on is not ready, and testing at realistic traffic needs data that does not exist yet.
solution: A terminal interface where an LLM chooses which runtime variables to probe. Once probes are attached, values can be changed on the fly to simulate a database or traffic, changes are reported back in plain language, and work is sent through a rule-based LLM router that picks cheaper or stronger text and image models.
demo_moment: Team-described: a frontend behaves as if its database exists, because Puppeteer feeds it data from inside the runtime.

why_it_stood_out.claim: One of 12 finalists among 261 submissions, and winner of the Warp developer-tool prize.
Built from a pain the whole team had felt: being blocked by an unfinished backend.
Routes calls across text and image models by rule to keep costs down as the tool iterates.
A developer tool judged by a panel heavy with founders and engineers: the problem needs no setup for this audience.

lessons: At a builder-heavy event, a tool for the judges' own daily pain can reach the finals without a consumer story.
